Kuvitus: talvinen ratapiha metsän keskel: Illustration: a winter railway yard in the middle of a forest on a bright day. On the left a reddish-brown covered goods wagon rolls to the right, with motion lines behind it. On the right stands an identical wagon that the rolling wagon is about to couple with. Above the tracks are the masts and the contact wire of an electrified railway, and in the background spruce forest and snowbanks.
Kaavakuva, nopeudet ja palkit mittakaava: Diagram, velocities and bars to scale. At the top, before the collision: the left wagon moves to the right at 1.6 m/s, blue arrow, and the right wagon is at rest. Below it, after the collision: the wagons are coupled and move together at 0.80 m/s, an arrow half as long. At the bottom are bars. The total momentum is the same before and after, 51 200 kilogram metres per second. The kinetic energy is 41 kJ before and 20 kJ after; the missing half has been transformed into internal energy of the buffers and couplings.
Kuvaaja: pysähtymismatka s p metreinä lä: Graph: the stopping distance s p in metres as a function of the initial speed v 0 in kilometres per hour. Seven black points at speeds of 30–90 km/h, distances from 12.5 m to 72 m. An upward-bending dashed curve passes through the points: the distance grows faster than the speed, so a straight line does not fit the points.
Kuvaaja: suure s p jaettuna v 0:lla seku: Graph: the quantity s p divided by v 0 in seconds as a function of the initial speed v 0 in metres per second. Seven black points at speeds of 8.3–25 m/s, values from 1.50 s to 2.88 s. A rising straight line is fitted to the points and extended as a dashed line to zero speed, where it crosses the vertical axis at about 0.86 s. Two points of the line are circled, (10 m/s; 1.66 s) and (25 m/s; 2.86 s), from which the slope of about 0.080 s²/m is read.
Käsitekartta. Ylhäällä solmu säilymislai: Concept map. At the top is the node conservation laws: energy and momentum. Three branches lead down from it. Energy: kinetic energy E k = half m v squared, potential energy E p = m g h and the work–energy principle, in which the initial mechanical energy plus the work done by other forces equals the final mechanical energy. Momentum: p = m v as vectors, the impulse–momentum principle impulse I = delta p, and conservation of momentum in a collision. Applications: in a collision momentum is conserved but kinetic energy only in an elastic one, the stopping distance is the reaction distance plus the braking distance, and the power of a hydropower plant is eta rho Q g h.
